newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian telecoms regulator sees investor confidence.
newsitem.headline: Indian telecoms regulator sees investor confidence.

text.p: Investor confidence in India's telecommunications sector is set to rise following the establishment of a clear policy regime, the chairman of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) said on Thursday.

"Snags and teething problems will no doubt be there. But all the inputs in ensuring investor confidence are there," S.S. Sodhi, who heads the three-member authority, told a seminar on telecommunications regulations.
"The next couple of years will see India rank among the major players in the world," Sodhi said.

The TRAI began operations on March 26, fulfilling a key demand for foreign investors who entered India to offer mobile and basic telephone services under an economic liberalisation programme launched in 1991.

Experts estimate India needs $60 billion in private investment to bring its telecommunications network to the level of countries like Brazil and Malaysia, which have six lines per 100 citizens compared to one for 100 in India.
Foreign investors have hailed the establishment of the regulator as a key step in assuring investors of a mechanism to ensure fair competition.
